These results could be used for proposing a novel model which could determine the quality using selected objective metric without need to do subjective tests.

articleTitle: Evidence of urban segregation from mobile phone data: A case study of Novi Sad
abstract: The segregation is a complex phenomenon driven by the demographic composition of the population, socioeconomic factors and underlying configuration of the geographic space. Here, we focused on segregation over 24 hours that occurs during one day inferred through the mobility of people. We utilized mobile phone data from telecom provider to estimate population mobility and explore patterns of segregation in the city. We used city's districts as spatial units for measuring segregation and quantified mobility between districts from call detail records data for the municipality of Novi Sad provided by Telecom Serbia. Following indices were calculated: Gini, Information Theory, Moran and Duncan Dissimilarity Index. Obtained results unveiled when and where the segregation is low and when and where it reaches high values. This served us to classify the districts based on their segregation level.

articleTitle: Processor Transformation for Integrated VoIP Soft-Switches
abstract: For a proprietary VoIP soft-switch product road map, it is planned to provide a service model as independent of hardware and compatible with NFV. Currently, Call Agent Core component of VoIP soft-switch and associated applications are compiled with Motorola PowerPC processor. The aim here is to port from Motorola PowerPC to Intel X86 processor architecture. In this study, requirement analysis and design items about Call Agent Core component are described.

articleTitle: Key Enablers to Deliver Latency-as-a-Service in 5G Networks
abstract: In the early 4G deployments, mobile communication providers have been focusing on connectivity technologies to meet the coverage and capacity needs of the users. With the advent of 5G, however, new value-added services including Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality (AR/VR), Mission Critical (MC) applications need to be supported. Open Radio Access Network (RAN) together with network slicing technology has been envisioned as one of the important solutions to realize Ultra Reliable Low Latency Communication (URLLC) services in 5G. The paper explores a novel framework and its under-pinning key enablers to deliver the ultra-low latency specifications for various 5G verticals including Smart Cities, Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and MC Services.

articleTitle: Using Optical IoT Sensing for Detrended Fluctuation Analysis of Skin Blood Pulsation during Visual Stimulation Task
abstract: This paper considers optical IoT sensing for the analysis of cardiovascular state. It is used for skin blood pulsation, i.e. photoplethysmography (PPG) signals acquisition and analysis using DFA (detrended fluctuation analysis) approach. Visual stimulus has been performed during the acquisition process. The results showed that DFA based spectra can be useful in further monitoring of the PPG signals. Analysis was performed using signals recorded from eight young volunteers.

articleTitle: Safety in Automotive Industry: ISO 26262 Compliant Unit Testing
abstract: Automotive and many industrial equipment, in most cases, have as a requirement a compliance to functional safety standards. Looking back in the past, there are multiple events, that have led to what we now call the functional safety standards. One such accident, which resulted in 167 dead, was the Piper Alpha offshore drilling platform. Unfortunately, it is impossible to completely avoid accidents, but what one wants to achieve is to reduce the consequences of such events. This paper is an attempt to explain how important functional safety is for automotive industry. Furthermore, we discuss how ISO 26262 can be applied to buses, trucks, trailers and semi-trailers with the main focus on the ISO 26262 compliant unit testing.

articleTitle: Consensus-based Localization by Using Array of Antennas on a Fixed-Wing UAV
abstract: A novel localization scheme, based on RSSI, is developed to make a fixed winged UAVs localize or track a target. Previous RSSI based localization methods require fingerprinting, knowledge about the transmitted power from the source as well as antenna and channel characteristics to apply the propagation loss formula. However, the proposed method in this paper only compares the received powers by antennas on a linear array and applying a control algorithm to ensure the consensus on received power, then find the location of the device.

articleTitle: Logical Synthesis and Circuitry of Digital Current Circuits: Polynomial Approach
abstract: The design basis of current circuits in Boolean and linear algebras are considered. An unconventional method for the synthesis of digital current circuits (DCCs) is proposed, which is based on the mathematical apparatus of linear algebra. Linear equations and circuitry of the main types of logic elements are given. The advantages of the linear implementation of the DCC in comparison with the Boolean implementation are presented.

articleTitle: Impact Hardware Raid Solutions at the Data Distribution on Tactical Integrated Telecommunication and Computer Network
abstract: The work present examination and comparation the impact of implementing RAID 0, 1 i 5 for network server configuration disks at the Email file distribution time in tactical integrated telecommunications and computer network (ITCN) for military purposes. Disk performance and RAID solutions application to write and read data from the server disk are associated with a time average for data distribution in a network, which is determined with the method of network simulation using the program OPNET.

articleTitle: SDN as a Tool for Energy Saving
abstract: Software Defined Networking (SDN) is considered as a promising solution for optimizing network energy consumption. This paper analyzes possible energy savings that could be achieved by turning off underutilized network links. It presents the energy consumption of a real IP/MPLS network and issues that prevent IP/MPLS from being more energy efficient. The paper proposes the SDN as an approach with a global view of the network and easier link management. A small experiment shows how easy it is for SDN to monitor and shut down unneeded links. This could enable a significant energy saving when using an SDN solution.

articleTitle: Stick Buffer Cache v2: Improved Input Feature Map Cache for Reducing off-chip Memory Traffic in CNN Accelerators
abstract: Data movement between the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) accelerators and off-chip memory is critical with respect to the overall power consumption. Minimizing power consumption is particularly important for low power embedded applications. Specific CNN compute patterns offer a possibility of significant data reuse, leading to idea of using specialized on-chip cache memories which enable significant improvement in power consumption. However, due to unique caching pattern present within CNNs, standard cache memories would not be efficient. In this paper novel on-chip cache memory architecture, based on idea of input feature map striping, is proposed, which requires significantly less on-chip memory resources compared to previously proposed solutions. Experiment results show that the proposed cache architecture can reduce on-chip memory size by a factor of 16 or more, while increasing power consumption no more than 15%, compared to some of previously proposed solutions.

articleTitle: Robot Task Allocation based on Greedy-Face-Greedy Algorithm
abstract: Two new algorithms (GFGF1 and GFGF2) for event finding in wireless sensor and robot networks based on the Greedy-Face-Greedy (GFG) routing are proposed in this paper. The purpose of finding the event (reported by sensors) is to allocate the task to the closest robot to act upon the event. Using two scenarios (event in or out of the network) and two topologies (random and random with hole) it is shown that GFGF1 always find the closest robot to the event but with more than twice higher communication cost compared to GFG, especially for the outside of the network scenario. GFGF2 features more than 4 times communication cost reduction compared to GFG but with percentage of finding the closest robot up to 90%.

articleTitle: Sparsity-Driven Impulsive Noise Removal: A Discrete Hermite Transform Case Study
abstract: This paper revisits a sparsity-assisted approach for the detection and removal of impulsive noise. Originally inspired by a sparse signal reconstruction methodology, which minimizes concentration measures through the variations of values of missing samples, the considered approach can perform a blind detection of impulsive disturbances, while the reconstruction is supported by the advances in the compressive sensing theory. The assumption is that the signal is sparse in a particular transform domain, which is the standard condition guaranteeing the reconstruction in the compressive sensing context. As a case study, an orthogonal form of the discrete Hermite transform is considered. Numerical results support the presented theory, indicating the efficiency of the method even in the challenging case of disturbances within the range of the signal.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic Nature of the Convectionless Atmospheric Plasma Jets
abstract: The paper deals with the theoretical model of a so-called apokamp discharge. It is known as unique atmospheric pressure plasmajet generated without natural or artificial convection from the bending region of a pulsed- periodic gas discharge channel of a specific configuration. Based on the simplified oxygen plasma-chemical model here we give a theoretical explanation of the apokamp phenomenon for the first time. It was shown that the apokamp is a stable plasma jet having physical nature of a positive streamer, it arises when some specific electrodynamic conditions are satisfied.

articleTitle: Development of a linear antenna array on a flexible substrate
abstract: The paper describes the procedure for developing a flexible antenna configured for Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz. The substrate material is a polyamide film with the thickness of 125 μm, the dielectric constant of 3.4, and tanδ = 0.004. The characteristics obtained during the simulation and experiment are presented. In addition, an assessment was made of the effect of the bending of the antenna sheet on its characteristics. Antennas on a flexible substrate are much easier to transport (roll up), and they can also take the form of a surface relief on which they are mounted.

articleTitle: An Approach to Automatic Layout of Eclipse Papyrus Class Diagrams
abstract: The paper presents an algorithm for automatic layout of class diagrams. The presented algorithm efficiently and openly tries to lay out a diagram in the landscape format using a modified Sugiyama algorithm. The proposed algorithm is implemented as an Eclipse plug-in and works within Papyrus class diagram modeling projects.

articleTitle: Character Level Keyword Spotting in VoIP Networks
abstract: In this paper, we present results from keyword spotting experiments in a setup where a voice over IP network is interconnected with the GSM network. Voice samples are intercepted by the VoIP exchange, passed to a server running the keyword spotting algorithm, and presented to the user via a web interface.The keyword spotting algorithm uses long-short term memory cells, trained using connectionist temporal classification, for Romanian words, using the Heimdall corpus. To train the network for the VoIP context, we processed the corpus through an experimental VoIP network. We achieved an accuracy of 83% for the output of the neural network, measured using the Levenshtein distance. However, the network is still training at the time we write this report, and the value of the loss function is still decreasing.

articleTitle: Estimation of Feasiblity of Using Bus Topology in Ttethernet Networks
abstract: Currently, TTEthernet supports 2 topologies: Star and Ring. Network components that can be found in TTEthernet network are switches and end systems. In this paper, we discussed about possibilities for using Hub topology in TTEthernet networks. The concept of TTEthernet operation is described, as well as necessary adaptations to be done for Hub topology support. Alongside with that, advantages and lacks of this approach are discussed, whence we can conclude whether this topology is acceptable at all in domain of TTEthernet networks applications. It is shown that reliance of the complete TTEthernet network only to bus topology is not a good option, because of lower fault-tolerant abilities. Possible application could be a mixed-topology, where bus topology will be used for low-critical traffic, while star of ring topology will be used for high-critical traffic.

articleTitle: Objective Assessment of Noise Presence in Diagnostic Radiographic Images
abstract: Objective evaluation of the effect of noise on diagnostic image quality of radiographic (X-ray) images provides an opportunity for autonomous elimination of noise and optimisation of overall quality of such imagery that meets the requirements of radiologists. Four objective measures of the effect of noise on the quality of diagnostic images are described in this paper. The aim of the metrics is to correspond as closely as possible to the quality assessments made by radiological diagnosticians. Of the proposed metrics, analysis of local coherence gives the best results, primarily for calcified tissue images, such as spine, hand and knee images.

articleTitle: Using NASL based Superscripts to measure System Security through Analyzing and Organizing attacks
abstract: Vulnerability scanning is a very important aspect in computer network security management towards prevention of system intrusions. To this end, Nessus is a worldwide accepted such tool involving state of the art techniques. The goal of this research is to analyze the principles of vulnerability scanning using Nessus and, more importantly, to model configurations and architectures of computer networks for efficiently employing Nessus towards formalizing vulnerability scanning evaluations. Most importantly, the contribution of the herein research is to provide a superscript based framework for such a vulnerability analysis of a small to medium enterprise.

articleTitle: Bulk Mode Encryption Devices Modification for Usage of Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: In this paper we describe a concept for modification of high capacity bulk mode (layer 1) cryptographic device that is originally designed for pre-shared key distribution to adopt quantum key distribution system. The main goal is to achieve reliable session key agreement suitable to operate at extreme bit rates without unnecessary frequent key agreement protocols, like commonly used Diffie-Helman. The architecture of solution is designed to achieve high encryption speed and maximal level of security is described in details. It is designed by utilizing field programmable gate array (FPGA) technology at gate level, bios-only microcontroller and Linux based embedded computer.

articleTitle: Estimating similarity between differently compiled procedures using neural networks
abstract: Dual licensing is a form of licensing where the same software product can be used under two different licenses. One license is usually free but introduces major restrictions on the usage of the software product, while the other allows a greater degree of freedom in using it, but at a specified monetary price. Although this form of licensing has a lot of benefits, one of its drawbacks is the increased possibility of license violation and copyright infringement. This paper deals with the problem of detecting a certain procedure from the source code in a set of disassembled binary procedures. The problem is made more difficult by not knowing which compiler was used to produce the binaries. The paper proposes an approach that falls into the category of Siamese neural networks and uses a combination of LSTM and DNN architectures. The proposed approach is evaluated independently on a dataset, as well against some of the currently available solutions.

articleTitle: Implementation of NETCONF Client in C++ Programming Language for Software Defined Networks
abstract: With the emerge of the software-defined networking paradigm, the Internet Engineering Task Force has standardized a new network configuration management protocol called NETCONF. Besides all features required for configuration management, the NETCONF is suitable for time-sensitive networking, since it provides event notification, validation capabilities, and filtering mechanisms. Knowing all of this, there must be a NETCONF client developed in any programming language running on any platform. However, there is no NETCONF client developed in C++ programming language for both Windows and Linux. In this article, such an implementation is described.

articleTitle: Multi-Functional Active RC-Filter (BPF, LPF, HPF, RF) for Designing Specialized Gate-Array Master Chip and Frequency Selection Devices
abstract: We have developed and investigated the multi-functional active RC-filter's (ARCF) architecture on base of three differential difference amplifiers (DDA) and its modifications, which implement low pass filter (LPF), high pass filter (HPF), band pass filter (BPF) and rejection filter (RF). We have done a mathematical analysis for ARCF's circuit variants, which allow their parametric synthesis. There are results of LPF's, HPF's, BPF's and RF's computer simulation in MicroCap on DDAs' models AD830, which are implemented due to signal source's switch to one of six inputs and three outputs, from which this signal is outputted. The suggested ARCF is advanced for selection devices' development on specialized gate-array master chips. The proposed ARCF's architecture is special, because the pole Q-factor adjustment does not result in transfer ratio's and pole frequency's change.

articleTitle: A Testbed Implementation of Localization in Wireless Heterogeneous Networks
abstract: This paper considers a WiFi based indoor localization algorithm for heterogeneous networks (HetNets). The given localization algorithm is based on the better modeling of the signal propagation in the wireless environment and proposed in the literature for homogeneous networks. Those studies prove the performance improvement of the lognormal mixture shadowing model over the classical shadowing models for homogeneous networks. Based on this, we extend those results to heterogeneous networks and test the proposed algorithm with experimental setup. The testbed implementation confirms that the taking the information from multiple networks into account shows better localization performance than the individual networks.

articleTitle: Exploring possibilities to exploit QFD method in telecommunication service design: the case of business customer
abstract: Satisfaction of customer requirements with proper telecommunication service design is a challenging for the operators. In the core of the problem is the question how to relate engineering characteristics of a service with customer desires in order to offer a solution that sets a balance between the demand and the supply side. This is particularly challenging in the case of business customers where predefined solutions, often offered by the telecommunications operators, may fail to fulfill customer's expectations and make vulnerable the operator's competitiveness. In this paper, we evaluate a method for service design built upon listening to the voice of customers, Quality Function Deployment (QFD). Using L3VPN service design as a case study, we go through the main steps of QFD implementation and offer signposts for successful implementation.

articleTitle: Research of Energy-Saving Wireless Self-Organizing Multy-Protocol Network for Internet of Things
abstract: The current level of wireless device development makes it possible to use a cheap wireless interface in almost any field of electronics, where previously mainly wired solutions were used. Most of the new devices are wireless, mobile, or wearable with varying degrees of autonomy. A large number of structures, buildings and private facilities are equipped with wireless security systems, fire alarms, wireless sensors for metering water, electricity, gas, etc. Many facilities additionally use lots of wireless devices for monitoring and controlling, including wireless relays, locks, video surveillance. We considered the operating protocols of the Internet of things and selected hardware solutions, which are the most affordable and popular for research. Since the goal is to build an arbitrary network, we considered methods for implementing self-organizing networks based on selected hardware devices and protocols.

articleTitle: Enhanced-Gain Dual-Polarized Slot Antenna with a Frequency Selective Surface
abstract: -In this manuscript, the design of a dualport/dual-polarized slot antenna with improved gain characteristic is proposed for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. The antenna design contains a diamond-ring slot radiator fed by two independently arrow-shaped microstrip feeding lines which can exhibit a polarization diversity characteristic. A low-cost FR-4 dielectric (ε= 4.4, δ= 0.02) is used as the substrate. In order to increase the gain characteristic of the antenna a 10×10 single-layer frequency selective surface (FSS) is employed below the dual-polarized slot antenna. The unit cell of the proposed FSS contains a square-ring radiator with a protruded circular-ring strip. A maximum gain of 9 dBi with less than 3 dB variation is obtained over the UWB frequency band. The characteristics of the dual-polarized UWB slot antenna with and without the FSS were examined using simulations and good simulation results have been obtained.

articleTitle: Generic Pseudorandom Sequence Generator Based on Permutations
abstract: In this article model of the pseudorandom sequence generator based on the permutations and parametrized by the two pseudorandom sequences is defined. For the proposed generator sufficient conditions for the output sequence uniform distribution are defined. Also independence between parametrization sequences and output sequence are proven.

articleTitle: One Solution for Preparing an Environment for Automatic Testing of an Electronic Control Unit in the Car
abstract: A solution for preparing an environment for automatic testing of an electronic control unit in a car is presented. The goal is to provide individual execution of automatic test cases, due to the testing of a specific component, withput the need to execute all test cases of a single test module.

articleTitle: Breakdown features in functional devices of telecommunication systems
abstract: Functional elements operation study revealed that the failure cause of the telecommunication devices is a degradation of conductive buses and contact pads. Experimental and theoretical studies of breakdown processes that are leading to integrated circuit's destruction under electromagnetic radiation influence are presented.

Author Keywords: the transformation of electromagnetic radiation energy.

articleTitle: Towards the Fixed Length Redundancy Code
abstract: In our previous work we have defined an error-detecting code with a fixed length of the redundancy. The analysed code is defined using the algebraic structure quasigroup. In this paper we analyse the case when a linear quasigroup of order 4 is used for coding. We obtain the number of errors that the code surely detects when the length of the redundancy is 8, 12 and 16 bits. At the end, we give some properties and conclusions for the number of errors that the code surely detects.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of DDPSK Receiver for Applications in IoT Systems
abstract: We present an analytical approach in the analysis of the symbol error rate performance of the receiver for double differential phase-shift keying (DDPSK) signals transmitted over generalized fading channel. The analysis is applicable in modern Internet-of-Things (IoT) wireless systems where multipath fading and shadowing appear simultaneously, and where coherent detection is not applied. We use Fourier series method for determining symbol error probability in detecting multilevel DDPSK signals. We give the comparison of the error rate values for DDPSK and differential phase-shift keying (DPSK) formats in the presence of the carrier frequency offset caused by Doppler shift. This comparison is performed for different fading and shadowing severities and some conclusions are derived related to the application of these two modulation formats.

articleTitle: Parametric optimization of the CJFET Buffer Amplifier with Low Offset Voltage within the Range of Low Temperature
abstract: A new design of a buffer amplifier (BA) on complementary junction field-effect transistors (CJFET) is investigated and optimized for practical use as a part of IP modules and analog ICs operating in severe conditions (exposure to low temperatures and penetrating radiation). The optimal parameters of the BA elements are chosen in the LTspice simulation software, with low temperature models CJFET were creating and using multi-criteria optimization algorithm NSGA-II from the DEAP library. Besides, the offset voltage of the BA is selected as a priority parameter to be improved with limit on current consumption. It is important, for example, for constructing operational amplifiers (OA) with current negative feedback.

articleTitle: Aequor Tracer – Network Analysis Application
abstract: This article presents the principles and algorithms used in our application, which we have developed to analyze network traffic. The two main parts of the application are geolocation service and traffic behavior analysis. Data are collected from NetFlow and PCAP (Packet Capture). For the behavior analysis, we us e our new proposed method using recalculation of traffic to the lifetime domain and clustering algorithm for deciding a similarity of lifelines. For the geolocation, we use an intersection method.

articleTitle: TETRA Based Secure Voice Communication Solution in Non-Developed Regions
abstract: In this paper we present a solution for secure voice communication for government institutions, suitable for deployment in non-developed regions which suffer from bad mobile network coverage, problems with power supply and relatively frequent acts of criminal activities and terrorism. The main emphasize of this paper is that TETRA, as a system designed for operation in crisis situations, could also be used for small scale deployment, rather than region or country level solution. As an example we gave preliminary use case of similar system deployment on randomly chosen area based on publicly available data about non-developed regions.

articleTitle: Developing an approach to summarizing the flows of security events to identify attacks in the network of telecommunication service providers
abstract: This study aims to develop a combined attack detection approach based on analysis of node state chains, as well as analysis of time delays within the network. The proposed algorithm allows you to determine the entry point to the network through which the attack began. Based on binary logistic regression, nodes with suspicious activity are identified and using the genetic algorithm to determine their belonging to the type of attack that takes place on the first studied node. As part of an experimental study, the effectiveness of the developed approach for identifying attacks in the network of telecommunication service providers was evaluated, which shows a sufficiently high determination accuracy, as well as good performance on large network topologies.

articleTitle: Sofrware Implementation and Analysis of NU-FBMC
abstract: In this paper an implementation of Nu-FBMC (Nonuniform Filter Bank Multicarrier) signal is presented, whose cyclic features are examined for the first time. The displayed graphics are obtained by simulations in MATLAB and they show outstanding cyclic features, which is important for the use in spectrum sensing in the process of joined detection and classification of signal.

Author Keywords: Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing/Offset Quadrature Amplitude Modulation

articleTitle: Implementation of NTP Protocol in an Isolated Corporate Network
abstract: Nowadays time synchronization presents a crucial part of infrastructure in any distributed system. A request for precise time synchronization of teleprotection equipment in the transmission network of the Serbian transmission system operator (JSC EMS), was generated due to the need for more precise analysis of the devices status and events that conditioned sending of teleprotection commands, as well as their time positions. The solution had to be developed in accordance with the current state of the transmission network, as well as the required reliability and accuracy for precise analysis of teleprotection events. The greatest challenge was implementation of standard time synchronization protocol on a loaded embedded processor system. The paper presents the overview of the realization including measurement methods and results.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Phased Array 5G Smartphone Antenna for Cognitive Cellular Networks
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a new reconfigurable dipole antenna array for cognitive 5G cellular networks. The single-element of the design contains a dipole radiator along with a pair of spiral resonators (SRs) at both sides of the substrate. The reconfigurability characteristic of the antenna is achieved by employing two active elements (PIN diodes) connecting the tips of the dipole arms and the spiral resonators. In the simulations, the rectangular copper sheets are excluded to approximate the cases with a turned on and off switch. The frequency response of the antenna can be switched to operate at 18 and 32.5 GHz while maintaining the main resonance at 25 GHz. In addition, the radiated beam directions can be reconfigured to broadside and end-fire modes. Using the proposed design, radiation properties of a smartphone antenna with a 1 × 8 linear dipole array have been investigated and satisfactory results have been achieved. The obtained results show that the proposed reconfigurable dipole antenna array fulfills the general requirements in cognitive cellular networks.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Statistical Correlation in the Context of Multi-Look SAR Tomography
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar Tomography successfully exploits the coherent processing principle, allowing for a precise long-term monitoring of the analyzed scenes. A challenging aspect is represented by the detection of the points which offer reliable estimates of the scene's parameters. Multi-looking processing-averaging of multiple points contributions-has proved to significantly improve the performances of the detection process. The derivation of the likelihood ratios exploited for the identification of stable targets implies the statistical modelling of the averaged looks. The analysis conducted in this work on a real dataset of acquisitions confirms that the assumed uncorrelated model of the data vectors is the most appropriate one.

articleTitle: Storage performance analysis of iSCSI and Fibre Channel protocol
abstract: In this paper we tested the performance of two different network protocols iSCSI and Fiber Channel. The performance analysis relies on the comparison of the flow velocity between these two protocols, i.e. the speed of the disks where the initiators are iSCSI and FC. Thus, for such comparison analysis, one of the tested disks was plugged in via the iSCSI initiator, while the other was connected via Fiber Channel. The testing procedure relies on the use of the HD Tune Pro tool and includes disk analysis in Random Read, Random Write, Sequential Read, and Sequential Write. The obtained results show significantly better performance of the Fiber Channel compared to the iSCSI.

articleTitle: Correcting the Chromatic Dispersion of a Fronthaul Fiber Link in Millimeter-Wave Radio -over-Fiber Networks
abstract: Fulfilling the requirements of 5G NR, the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation mobile network equipped with advanced features such as network MIMO and multi-user diversity, new and more advanced fronthaul design is needed. Analog radio over fiber has been proposed to provide high bandwidth signals with simple receiver architecture from the baseband unit to the remote radio heads. At such a high data rate, fiber distortions, i.e. chromatic dispersion, become significant and need to be compensated. Here we study applying a simple optical filter implemented by means of fiber Bragg grating technique and evaluate its performance for various scenarios through numerical simulations. It is evident from the observed results that the proposed approach is effective in increasing the reach and providing reliable communication with simple implementation.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Wireless Automation Module for Diesel Engines
abstract: This paper describes the design of wireless CAN protocol with the aim to replace existing wired CAN protocol communication between the Smart NOx sensor on diesel engines and the Engine Control Unit (ECU). Wireless industrial automation becomes essential in modern industry with the emerge of 5G networks and the IoT. Besides the advantages of wireless nodes in automation systems, there are many real challenges. Several practical design challenges have been successfully addressed in this paper.

articleTitle: Harmonic Beam Steering through Dual-Phase Variable Pulse Amplitude Switching Strategy in Time Modulated Linear Arrays
abstract: Time Modulated Arrays (TMA) use radio frequency (RF) switches, which are simpler and cheaper than traditional phase shifters for the beamforming. Because of the RF switches, in addition to the main radiation, the harmonic components, which affect the efficiency of the array are generated at multiples of the modulation frequency. In this study, dual-phase variable pulse amplitude (DPVPA) excitation waveform is proposed which can be amplified and steered to the desired harmonic component rather than the first harmonic component. Furthermore, the proposed method provides a significant advantage in signal bandwidth as higher-order harmonics can be exploited.

articleTitle: Optimization of ANN input parameters used in electric field level prediction model
abstract: This paper presents optimization of existing ANN (Artificial Neural Network) electric field level prediction model in a microcellular environment. Optimization is achieved using feedforward neural networks. The analysis showed that choosing optimal input parameters gives a better quality prediction than when considering all input parameters used by existing model. Optimization has been achieved in terms of increasing the accuracy of prediction and reducing the complexity of the model itself.

articleTitle: QoE and Video Quality Evaluation for HTTP Based Adaptive Streaming
abstract: Video quality demanded by the end user must result in the best possible Quality of Experience (QoE). QoE assesment as well as its integration into video streaming algorithms is a complex problem that demands a comprehensive design of subjective databases and video quality metrics. This paper presents an analysis of different video quality metrics and their usability for QoE measurement for HTTP based adaptive streaming (HAS). To compare the metrics, the LIVE-NFLX-II database is used.

articleTitle: Compact Directional Coupler for Centimeter and Millimeter Wavelength Ranges
abstract: In this paper the compact directional couplers for centimeter and millimeter frequency bands are investigated. Using the NI-AWR Design Environment software, four layouts of miniaturized couplers were synthesized at the central frequencies of 1, 10, 20 and 30 GHz, which dimensions are smaller by 77.75%, 58.8%, 48.4% and 49.4%, respectively, in comparison to the standard designs. Miniaturization was carried out based on equivalent replacement of quarter-wave segments with low-pass filters of the 3rd order.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Spiral Antenna Properties for Research the Brain Radiation in the Microwave Range
abstract: This paper investigates a planar single-arm spiral antenna used to measure human brain radiation in the frequency range 3-5 GHz. The investigation was carried out using numerical modeling (finite elements method) by employing ANSYS Electromagnetics Suite 19.2. In this software, the model of brain tissues and antenna was built. An optimization of antenna parameters was carried out to obtain the best matching and sensing depth. Frequency dependence of antenna input impedance, reflection coefficient was computed, and also a volume distribution of electromagnetic field in the head tissue was obtained. An influence matching layer to antenna characteristics is investigate in case of deviation of electrical parameters of the head tissue top layers. The matching layer is located between the spiral antenna plane and the surface of the head. To validate the obtained results, an additional simulation was carried out by using another software EM simulator.

articleTitle: Modeling and Implementation of an Economical System for Regulating Vehicle Interior Temperature
abstract: Modeling and implementation of an economical system for regulating vehicle interior temperature based on fuzzy logical control which is responsible for collecting, processing and distribution of data. Algorithm controlling which satisfies optimal consumption criteria as well as criteria of minimum time delay for temperature set point reachment. This scientific paper shows modeling, system implementation as well as system testing.

articleTitle: 3D Audio Post-Processing Module on DSP Platform
abstract: Object-based 3d audio has attracted many audio content makers and audio engineers. This kind of audio signal gives the listener a more realistic sound effect around him than, for instance, stereo or surround. An audio object is a type of signal which consists of two parts – PCM (pure audio content) and metadata (additional information on how objects should be rendered). A component that handles object-based signals is called object renderer which adjusts audio content based on metadata. In this paper, an evaluation of object renderer on DSP platform is reported with an example of assembly implementation within the MPEG-H system.

articleTitle: Agile Software Integration in Telecommunications — a Case Study
abstract: Agile methodologies changed the way of software development in the last decades. However, there is still struggling with the implementation of agile methods in environments such as the telecommunications industry with its long lasting projects in complex and large system set-ups. In this paper, we present a survey on agile software projects in telecommunications and comparable organizations and a case study of a multi-year software integration project and its transition from traditional project execution to agile methods at an Austrian mobile network operator. Including all pitfalls and failures.

articleTitle: PARATA: A Routing Strategy in VANET for CO2 Emissions Reduction
abstract: Vehicular networks represent an important research filed in the scientific community. The interest in this topic is confirmed also from the many works in literature. The focus of this paper is to optimize the traffic flowing in a vehicular environment with vehicle-2-roadside capability in order to resolve congestion and emission issues. The proposed idea is based on the better management of road-side units, that collect road information and then have the ability of changing traffic flows in order to exploit less congested roads. This management allows a system optimization, also in terms of Carbon Dioxide emissions reduction. We propose an algorithm able to perform re-routing and then reduce car CO2 emission. We show our simulative campaigns in order to prove the goodness of the proposal.

articleTitle: Building a Prototype Netcloudbook for User Activities-centered Social Network based on Booked Open-source and Docker Technology
abstract: The paper tackles the issue of building a user activities-centered social network that helps users to have benefit and enjoy activities in real life. The technical solution is based on an open-source and Docker technology on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP). The paper gives a comparison between some existing digital communities and proposes a relationship circles template.

articleTitle: Enhancement in P4 Language by Printing user Defined Messages in Behavioral Model Simulator
abstract: P4 is an open source, permissively licensed programming language used to program network devices, designed to enable protocol-independent packet forwarding. The language was originally described in a SIGCOMM CCR paper in 2014 titled “Programming Protocol-Independent Packet Processors” [1] - the alliterative name shortens to “P4”. This paper will introduce the P4 language, P4 compiler and new log_msg function [2][3] for printing user defined messages.

articleTitle: On Efficient Scheduling Schemes in Multiagent Wireless Sensor Networks Simulation Systems
abstract: Time notion is of paramount importance in a simulation process. What, how and when an event takes place in the simulation environment describes what how and when an event should take place in the real world and vice versa. The simulation tool of choice should provide the ability to minimize or even completely remove assumptions and operate with the highest time and synchronization accuracy as well as to minimize overheads of time management. In this paper we describe proper scheduling schemes that our proposed multiagent based WSN simulation system provides in order to handle time, and we evaluate the performance of the time controller in terms of agent population, synchronization and execution scenarios.

articleTitle: Collaboration network analysis of scientific production at UB-SEE
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the coauthors collaboration network based on research papers published in journals, where at least one author is affiliated to the University of Belgrade, School of Electrical Engineering (UB-SEE). We have extracted data from the institutional database and processed 2000 papers published in journals during the period from 2000 to 2017. After the initial refinement of the dataset we created and visualized the network of coauthors and carried out further analysis based on metrics specifically used for social network analysis.

articleTitle: Singularity Analysis for 3-DOF Reconfigurable Robots
abstract: A 3-DOF reconfigurable robot model is presented with the reconfigurable parameters related to the joint types and the selection of joint positive directions. The Jacobian matrix is developed using the Vukobratovié-Potkonjak's method, and the singularity regions are derived through the determinant of the related 3×3 Jacobian matrix. Eight groups of the 3-DOF kinematic structure (TTT, TTR, TRT, RTT, TRR, RTR, RRT, and RRR) are analyzed separately, and the singular configurations of each group are given in detail.

articleTitle: One application of Groebner’s basis to detection of bounding volume spheres collision
abstract: This paper gives overview of application of Groebner's basis on problem of object collision. Method presented in this paper solves some of problems related to algorithms of collision detection. To prove functioning of this method it was implemented in computer application and it has shown benefits and limitations of this method.

articleTitle: PHY Security Improvement of Wireless Sensor Networks in Presence of an Untrusted User
abstract: This paper proposes a new hybrid secure transmission scheme, TAS-SC-ZFB for wireless sensor networks (WSNs). This scheme uses transmit antenna selection (TAS) at the base station (BS) and adopts selection combining (SC) over legitimate nodes. Aditionally, zeroforcing beamforming (ZFB) is applied at the friendly jammer to confuse the effects of the eavesdropping node. Particularly, exact closed-form expressions for the secrecy outage probability (SOP) and the effective secrecy throughput are derived. Using these expressions, the optimal power allocation factor between the BS and jammer and optimal secrecy rate are obtained to minimize the SOP and maximize the secrecy throughput, respectively. Numerical results are used to validate the theoretical analysis and to compare with the existing state of the art.

articleTitle: Comparing simulation model for objective QoE video evaluation with real IPTV test scenario during appearance of packet losses
abstract: The aim of this paper is comparing a simulation model with real IPTV (Internet Protocol TeleVision) scenario in access network. In real IPTV scenarios, it is known that packet losses appear suddenly and might have an "explosive" character, especially in DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) case. In addition, these packet losses usually appear in groups and lead to huge degradation of the video service, which decreases customer's QoE (Quality of Experience) level. Hence, estimation of this degradation in access network is important and the paper explained one simulation model based on SSIM (Structural Similarity Index) analysis, which can be used as one perceptive video quality assessment by imitating a real environment with packet losses. To check this, we compared our simulation model with the real IPTV video distributed over DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) and exposed to different packet loss appearances.

articleTitle: Application of Telegraph Equation Soluton Telecommunication Signal Trasmission and Visualization in Matlab
abstract: Partial differential equations are a branch of engineering mathematics that in the last decades in the scientific field has played a very important role in solving certain engineering problems. In this paper, we have applied a kind of partial differential equations when examining the influence of microwaves. We have observed the phenomena occurring in one part of the electromagnetic spectrum in the frequency range of 1 GHz-100 GHz as an aggravating factor in signal transmission by telecommunication water, which was the starting point for research on this topic. The reason for isolating this area is contained in the specific technique that characterizes it. One of the types of partial hyperbolic equations is the telegraphic equation, whose solution eliminates problems related to the transmission line. The graphical interpolation of the telegraph equation is given in the Matlab Engineering Matrix Laboratory. Only the parts of mathematically important functions are derived in the paper and the final results are presented in order to represent our starting differential equation as telegraphic.

articleTitle: Testing Web Page Layouts Using Galen Framework Tests Generated By The Mockup Tool
abstract: The objective of this paper is to develop the tool which aids the implementation of test specifications for web page layout testing. The tool combines the process of user interface mockup design and implementation of tests. Generated test specifications are verified using two mutation testing operators. Mutation testing was also performed on referent test specifications generated by Galen Framework from goal web page dump files. Tests should detect mutations with a visual change on a web page. Additional image comparison of web page screenshots was performed to determine if there was a visual change. Verification showed that mockup test specifications are less precise than referent test specifications. Nonetheless, they also show fewer false-positive results. It was concluded that generated tests have some limitations, but they can be used as a starting point for writing more precise layout tests.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable 2.4GHz Power Amplifier for Polar Transmitters in 28nm FD-SOI CMOS technology
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated Power Amplifier (PA) for Polar Transmitter architectures. The proposed PA consists of two digitally controlled multi-cell stages with a reconfigurable output matching network in order to achieve the maximum output power regardless of the load impedance. More specifically, the first stage provides the synthesis of Amplitude and Phase signals of the polar transmitter and the second stage produces the final output power. The overall performance of the designed PA, is validated through extensive simulations for all Process, Voltage and Temperature variations (PVT/corners variations). With a 1. 8V supply voltage, the PA achieves an output power range from -4.6 to 14.2 dBm at 2. 4GHz. The design is performed in a 28nm Fully Depleted Silicon-On-Insulator (FD- SOI) CMOS technology and is suitable for 2. 4GHz applications.

articleTitle: Pattern Synthesis in Time Modulated Arrays via Offsetted Time Sequences
abstract: In this work, an approach based on nonuniform period variable pulse amplitude (VPA) switching strategy for pattern synthesis in time modulated arrays is presented. The approach utilizes optimization of on-time durations, switching frequencies and waveform amplitude by differential evolution (DE) algorithm for synthesizing desired sidelobe level (SLL), sideband level (SBL) and sideband radiation power (SRp). In the scope of the optimization procedure, 40 independent experiments are performed and the fastest slowest experiments are analyzed.

articleTitle: Integration of Google Game service with TV application on Android devices
abstract: In this paper we present integration of an existing android TV application with the Google Game services. The goal is to register and evaluate user interactions (channel change, viewed movie, long channel viewing, recorded events, etc.) in order to give the user a sense of playing a video game. By creating this model, the user should be encouraged by defining the achievements to use certain options as much as possible. The idea of work is to present this model as a potential marketing approach where achievements could be used to place specific content.

articleTitle: Source code generators for ADAS feature deployment in context of ROS and adaptive AUTOSAR applications
abstract: Fast development of autonomous vehicles comes with many challenges. One of biggest platform wise challenges is parallel development of Adaptive AUSOSAT platform and application that run on it. Use of source code generators was chosen to solve this problem. This paper will give one solution of using ROS features to allow running adaptive application on still developing platform using source code generators. To understating why specific ROS concepts are used, overview of ROS concepts and Adaptive AUTOSAR platform is given in this paper. Use of IDL to describe interfaces and source code generators to generate C++ code allows programmers to focus only on important features, forgetting about implementation details and faster development of more portable software.

articleTitle: Comparison of schemes with distributed parameters and II scheme of circuits that are closed by nonlinear inductance
abstract: The paper presents original algorithm and adapted program of psb11phasline-MATLAB Simulink for modeling the transient processes of a part of network formed by a source, a line with distributed parameters and a nonlinear element-energy transformer for powering active load. In the simulation process on elements with given parameters and frequency, a comparison of the replacement schemes used so far in electrical circuit theory has been performed. The program for transient process simulation, obtained voltage and current diagrams confirm the applicability of the model of set algorithm for calculation.

articleTitle: High Quality Differential Speech Signal Coding Based on Backward Adaptation Technique
abstract: This paper presents simple speech coding algorithm, based on differential coding and backward adaptive quantization. Both coding techniques are based on backward adaptation, meaning that for the coding of current speech signal sample the information from the previously coded samples are used. Paper also emphasis on the quantizer design and on the iterative optimal support limit determination. Experimental results indicate that our low complexity algorithm complies with the G. 712 Recommendation for high quality speech coding, while using only 6 bits per sample. Additionally, higher objective output signal quality in comparison to similar complexity coding algorithms indicate that the proposed algorithm can be indeed successfully applied in speech signal coding.

articleTitle: Nova metoda za detekciju copy move promena na slikama [Not available in English]
abstract: Zahvajući stalnom razvoju tehnologija, mobilnih telefona i digitalnih kamera, upotreba digitalnih fotografija je zastupljena u svakodnevnom životu. Koriste se kao izvori informacija, ali éesto i kao potrekpljujući dokazi u forenziékim istraživanjima, kao dokazi na sudu, novinarstvu i sliéno. Izmena sadržaja takvih slika je postala jako jednostavna, preko odreêenih softverskih alata, tako da ne možemo biti sigurni u originalnost slike. Promene nastaju tako što se doda ili ukloni odreêeni sadržaj slike, ili se od više slika pravi jedna slika, a sve u cilju pogrešnog prenosa informacija. Iz tih razloga je znaéajno razvijati nove metode za detekciju takvih promena. Jedna od najviše zastupljenih promena jeste tkz. CMFD (Copy Move Forgery Detection). Promene nastaju tako što se deo slike kopira i nalepi na neki drugi deo unutar iste slike. Takve promene se naknadno mogu skalirati, rotirati, višestruko kopirati i sliéno. Obzirom da su kopirani i nalepljeni delovi sa iste slike, njihova detekcija postaje dodatno složenija, jer su karakteristike kopiranih i nalepljenih delova jako sliéne (komponente šuma, temperature boja, sjajnost, i sliéno). Multifraktali kao i multifraktalni spektar su se pokazali dobro u samoj analizi slika, segmentaciji i izdvajanju odreêenih karakteristika slike. Mogu da opisiju signal lokalno, preko vrednosti odgovarajućeg Hölder-ovog eksponenta, i globalno, preko vrednosti raspodele tih koeficijenata – multifraktalnog spektra. Stoga je predložena nova metoda za detekciju CMFD promena na slikama, zasnovana na odreêenim parametrima multifraktalnog spekra, kao i nekim statistiékim parametrima. Slika od interesa se deli na nepreklapajuće blokove fiksnih dimenzija. Svaki blok se opisuje karakteristiénim vektorom, sastavljenim od parametara MF spektra i statistiékih paramatera. Za uparivanje blokova, pronalaženje duplikata i klasterovanje blokova u izmenjene i neizmenjene, predložena je nova semimetrika, zasnovana na metaheuristici. Preciznost predložene metode je potvrêena eksperimentalno, testiranjem slika iz javno dostupnih baza slika, kao i testiranjem slika generisanih za potrebe istraživanja. Parametri preciznosti detekcije jesu procenat taéne kao i procenat lažne detekcije, kao i preciznost i opoziv. Dobijeni rezultati pokazuju da predložena metoda daje znaéajno bolje rezultate u odnosu na rezultate koje su predstavili drugi autori. Takoêe, predložena metoda ima manju kompleksnost raéunanja, u odnosu na ostale metode (karakteristiéni vektor se sastoji od samo 7 deskriptora)..

articleTitle: BANG: The Barabashi-Albert Network Generator as a modeling automation tool
abstract: The development of a novel network protocol often requires significant testing efforts. One popular type of testing is computer simulation-based experimentation. However, creating the required model is not an easy task. On the one hand, such a model should be complex enough to reveal all the features of the protocol being tested. On the other hand, such models must be created quickly and easily so that researchers need not expend too much of their resources on them. This paper presents a tool designed to help in the modeling of computer networks. The BANG project (the Barabashi-Albert Network Generator) is focused on the creation of models of computer networks which exhibit the Barabashi-Albert topology. The rationale for choosing the Barabashi-Albert model as the basic algorithm for constructing computer network topologies is explained in this research. OMNeT ++ is used as the modeling environment, where OMNeT ++ is an open source software system distributed on the basis of a free license. In addition to all this, the present study describes an attempt to deploy this tool (BANG) on a cluster at Samara University.

articleTitle: Application system for indoor navigation
abstract: The paper describes a system consisting of two applications intended for institutions belonging to the field of tourism, such as museums and galleries. The first, client-side mobile application is intended for visitors to these institutions and aims to inform users in an interactive way about the contents of the objects in which they are located. The second application is a web-based platform that enables institution employees to enter and manage data that will be displayed to visitors on a mobile application.

articleTitle: Implementation of Smart Home Solution based on Internet of Things
abstract: With the advances in information and communication technologies, small tiny devices capable to sense the environment became cheap and affordable. This opens many new possibilities to design cheap and simple solutions for monitoring indoor and outdoor environments. In this paper, we have designed and developed a complete system based on Internet of Things technologies for indoor temperature regulation. The main contributions of this paper are: (1) to remotely regulate the temperature in a condominium-based apartment; and (2) to provide apartment temperature zoning in order to save energy. Our system combines state-of-the-art off-the-shelf hardware components and embedded software to create a contemporary solution.

articleTitle: Applying Event-Based Sending Intervals to Enable Low Energy OPC-UA on Sensor Nodes
abstract: Integrating typical wireless sensors into industrial control systems is a crucial task to realize the full potential of the Industrial Internet of Things (IoT). Many lightweight protocols exist for the use in the IoT context with a focus on energy efficient data transmissions. Industrial protocols on the other hand ensure reliable and timely transfer of data but typically at the cost of a higher energy consumption. In this paper, we analyze and compare one protocol from each category to determine the different energy consumption and then evaluate how different sending schemes can enhance the energy consumption of the industrial protocol. The goal is to reduce the energy consumption while keeping the relevant information under industrial constraints and enabling tuning to different scenarios. Our results show that these goals are achievable by applying event-based sending approaches. However, a good understanding of the process at hand is required to trade-off different constraints.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Work Window using a Unified Robot Model
abstract: This paper explores the work envelope and the work window for two 6 serial axis robot families using a unified robot model. The work envelope, or workspace, represents all possible positions which may be occupied by a mechanism during its normal range of motion (for all positions). The work window is the reachable region for any given end effector orientation and is a subset of the work envelope. It is not intuitive to define, and when assessing feasibility strategies for process planning scenarios, needs to be readily determined for various kinematic configurations. A methodology to determine the reach feasibility of a desired configuration set is presented in this research. The unified model developed using Maple and Matlab is presented. Several examples are shown to demonstrate the affect of twist angles on to the shape of a robot work window. This important kinematic property needs to be used in cases of robot selection and as a tool design feature.

articleTitle: Improvement of Hardware Firewall’s Data Rates by Optimizing Suricata Performances
abstract: Suricata is a high-performance, multi-threaded Network IDS, IPS and Network Security Monitoring engine that can monitor networks in real time to protect against attacks. With its diverse features, Suricata is the choice of modern Unified Threat Management (UTM) systems to help networks secure their boundaries. As the network capacity increases to 40Gbps and beyond, it becomes important to tune Suricata to provide a lossless detection to the network. This paper describes the different tunings that were done to Red Piranha's Crystal Eye appliances to achieve 60Gbps Suricata throughput. Suricata throughput, as described in this paper, defines the amount of data that can be handled by Suricata engine without any drops. We describe the hardware configurations as well as the Suricata configurations that can help achieve high detection rates. We have also added the test results for single NIC and dual NIC systems and discussed the impact of hardware on Suricata performance.

articleTitle: Modeling and Linearization of Active Phased Arrays with Non-uniform Power Distribution
abstract: This paper investigates the linearization of active antenna arrays with non-uniform power distributions, which is challenging for conventional linearization methods. A technique based on the nonlinearity consistencies existing among the PAs is proposed and the technique allows linearizing the whole array using a single pre-distortion signal. Simulation results with a four-element array using GaN PAs show that the proposed technique can improve the ACPRs of the PAs in the array by up to 16 dB.

articleTitle: A Media-Based Modulation Communication System Implementation Using Universal Software Radio Peripheral
abstract: Index Modulation (IM) techniques have become a popular research topic for the next generation communication systems due to their prominent spectral efficiencies. Media-Based Modulation (MBM) which can provide high data rates using multiple RF switching components like PIN diodes and fewer transmit antennas is one of the newest members of the IM family. It may be also a candidate for the physical layer of 6G cellular communication systems. In this study, we implement an MBM communication system that utilizes a reconfigurable antenna (RA) with the help of an embedded system and universal software radio peripherals (USRP) with LabVIEW. We also design the RA which is used at the transmitter. The designed RA has been manufactured on a printed circuit board (PCB) with an antenna driver circuit and the measurements related with its operability have been taken and validated. In order to switch the PIN diodes on the RA, we use an ARM-based microprocessor which carries the information to be transmitted. After the testbed is installed, the data transfer is accomplished by our MBM scheme successfully.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic-based scheduling of rail vehicles under reduced traffic flow conditions
abstract: Design of fuzzy logic system for traffic scheduling is presented for the case of bidirectional traffic of personal rapid transit rail vehicles under reduced traffic flow conditions due to obstruction, which mandates diverting of local traffic. The proposed traffic scheduling system has been verified against the conventional traffic control system under stochastic conditions of incoming traffic at both sides of the partially-obstructed traffic corridor under examination.

articleTitle: AB Class CJFET Dual-Input Stage for Low Temperature Analog ICs
abstract: We suggest original circuit of input differential stage (DS) of AB class on a base of complementary field effect transistors with p-n-junction (CJFET). The main application of the DS is low noise analog ICs for operation in low temperatures, including cryogenic temperatures. Special circuit design of DS static mode circuit design and its parametric optimization in LTspice simulation software provide relatively high stability of static mode of input CJFET in wide temperature rage. At the same time, DSs common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR). We show a possibility to update DS circuit design on CMOS transistors.

articleTitle: Time-Frequency Analysis of Ionospheric Whistler Signals
abstract: Time-frequency analysis of the ionospheric whistler signals is presented. Prior to the time-frequency analysis, disturbances caused by power-grid influence and ionospheric tweek and sferic signals are filtered using frequency domain and time domain filtering, respectively. Instantaneous frequency law of whistler signals is then estimated. S-method is used as a time-frequency representation in order to obtain highly concentrated representation without undesired crossterms. The presented method is applied to the real-life ionospheric signals.

articleTitle: Partial update of automobile software
abstract: This work describes one solution for partial update of automobile software. Partial update enables more flexibility of the AUTOSAR architecture, as the primary architecture for software development in automotive industry. It also enables changes and enhancement part of the automobile system, without compromising the functionality of the other parts, and with that it opens wide range of possbilities.

articleTitle: A Solution for Measuring Code Coverage during Automated Testing of an Electronic Circuit Unit
abstract: Code coverage provides information about quality of test cases. It provides information on how much code (object of testing) is executed. This paper offers a technical solution for acquiring information about code coverage of code which is running on an Electronic Circuit Unit.

articleTitle: DNN Based Expressive Text-to-Speech with Limited Training Data
abstract: Modern text-to-speech synthesis systems should deliver speech which is not just intelligible, but whose style corresponds to the domain in which synthesized speech is used. In this paper three approaches based on deep neural networks aimed at synthesis of expressive speech are presented: style code, model re-training and an architecture using shared hidden layers. Their usability is tested on a speech corpus with a limited amount of expressive speech data. A new architecture for transplanting speech styles is also presented and compared with a referent approach from literature.

articleTitle: An Overview of Novel Methods for ASEP Performance Evaluation Based on Q-Function Approximation
abstract: The closed-form expression for Q-function does not exist so it is necessary to develop its approximation in order to overcome the difficulties that might appear in diverse research areas. In this paper the authors are presenting overview of two improved models for Q-function approximation with wide applicability. The first one is based on Karagiannidis and Mils model and the second one is based on Borjesson model to obtain the desired improved form of Q-function approximation.

articleTitle: Organic Semiconductors in Optical Communications
abstract: In this paper organic and hybrid photonic components for the applications in integrated photonic circuits, fiber optic systems and wireless optical communications are reviewed. The review highlights positive aspects and drawbacks of current technologies and presents the possible solutions that organic materials offer.

articleTitle: Semantic Internet of Things Platforms-Examples of Two Different Approaches for Cloud Environment
abstract: This paper covers the semantic enabled Internet of Things (IoT) platforms, which include the author's previous research work as well as his future research directions. First, the extension of non-semantic IoT platforms based on publish-subscribe connectivity protocols is proposed to enable semantic interoperability. Second, a semantic IoT platform based on RDF triple store optimized for semantic sensor streams is presented, and its potential improvement using the latest achievements in data management is discussed.

articleTitle: Room sound field characterization and clustering using global multifractal parameters
abstract: This paper introduces one method for room sound field characterization and clustering and it presents part of the research carried out for the purpose of the doctoral dissertation. Room impulse response is the basic source of information in room acoustics. The algorithm provides impulse response characterization and clustering using global multifractal parameters. Large Deviation method is used in calculating the multifractal spectrum. The correlation between different multifractal parameters and room acoustic characteristics is determined. Clusters of impulse responses with identical acoustic characteristics are formed. The test results verify the usability of the proposed algorithm.
